title: Maximum Subarray Sum

concept.title: Best sum ending here
body: Among all blocks of consecutive elements, which one has the largest sum? Look at the best block that **ends at position i**. It is either the element `a[i]` alone, or the best block ending at `i - 1` extended by `a[i]`. If the earlier block has a negative sum, it only hurts, so we start fresh.

body.code:
cur = best = a[0]
for x in a[1:]:
    cur = max(x, cur + x)    # best block ending at this element
    best = max(best, cur)

body: This is **Kadane's algorithm**: one pass, two variables. The block must contain at least one element, so for an array of only negative numbers the answer is its largest (least negative) element.

statement: Given an array of `n` integers, find the largest sum of a non-empty block of consecutive elements.

examples.note: All numbers are negative: the best block is the single element -2.

hints: Think about the best block that ends at the current element.
It is either the element alone or the previous best block plus the element.
Keep the largest value of that "best ending here" over the whole pass.

input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

explanation: `cur` is the best sum of a block ending at the current element. A negative `cur` is dropped, which is what `max(x, cur + x)` does.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

cur = best = a[0]
for i in range(1, n):
    cur = max(a[i], cur + a[i])
    best = max(best, cur)
print(best)
